headline: Hiking Access Near Historic Trinity
reservation: The trail itself does not currently require a permit for day use, but local accommodations in Trinity and Port Rexton are often booked months in advance. Visitors should verify current trail maintenance status with the Skerwink Trail Conservation Association before arrival. Special events in the region may impact local parking availability.

days.title: Coastal Cliffs and Sea Stacks

stops.name: Skerwink Trailhead
stops.detail: Begin the loop from the designated parking area near the church in Port Rexton to follow the coastal perimeter.

stops.name: Skerwink Rocks
stops.detail: Observe the dramatic sea stacks and look for whales or icebergs depending on the specific month of your visit.

days.driving: Walking route; allow 3 to 4 hours for the 5.3km loop depending on photography stops.
days.note: The cliffside sections have steep drops; stay on marked paths to avoid eroding edges.

days.title: Historic Trinity Architecture

stops.name: Lester-Garland House
stops.detail: Tour this reconstructed brick dwelling to understand the 18th-century merchant history of the region.

stops.name: Gun Hill Trail
stops.detail: Ascend for a bird's-eye view of the Trinity harbor, offering a different perspective than the Skerwink cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local transit between Trinity and Port Rexton; roads are narrow.
days.note: Trinity is a living museum; respect private residential areas while exploring the heritage buildings.

days.title: Bonavista Peninsula Landmarks

stops.name: Cape Bonavista Lighthouse
stops.detail: Visit this iconic provincial historic site at the tip of the peninsula, known for puffin sightings nearby.

stops.name: Dungeon Provincial Park
stops.detail: View the massive natural sea arch carved by the Atlantic waves, located a short drive from the lighthouse.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour each way for the drive to Bonavista; conditions vary with coastal fog.
days.note: Wind speeds at the Cape can be significantly higher than in the sheltered harbors of Trinity.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: The primary lot in Port Rexton is small; avoid parking on narrow residential shoulders to maintain emergency access. Use the overflow area if directed by local signage.

intel.title: Peninsula Coverage
intel.text: Signal is generally stable in Port Rexton but can be intermittent on the far side of the Skerwink loop. Download offline maps for the Bonavista backroads.

intel.title: Limited Station Count
intel.text: Fuel stations are sparse between Clarenville and Bonavista. Ensure your tank is sufficient before leaving the Trans-Canada Highway junction.

intel.title: Wildlife Windows
intel.text: Icebergs typically pass in late spring, while whales are more common in mid-summer. Puffin activity at nearby Elliston is most frequent from July through August.

intel.title: Terrain and Weather
intel.text: The trail includes stairs and boardwalks that can be slippery when wet. Coastal fog can move in rapidly, obscuring landmarks and dropping temperatures.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Gander or St. John's; stop for major grocery supplies in Clarenville as Trinity offers limited boutique options.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are ideal for the narrow streets of Trinity; RVs may find the historic core difficult to navigate.
plan.goldenHour: The Skerwink sea stacks catch the morning light beautifully, though sunrise timing shifts significantly across the Newfoundland summer.
